additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by the presence of one or more non-bizarre or plausible-sounding delusions lasting at least one month, in the relative absence of other psychotic features such as prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech, or marked negative symptoms. Outside of the delusional beliefs, cognitive functioning and behavior are often largely preserved, and overall functioning may remain relatively intact compared with schizophrenia. The content of the delusions can be persecutory, somatic, grandiose, jealous, or erotomanic, and individuals often come to clinical attention because of interpersonal conflict, occupational problems, or legal/organizational involvement stemming from their fixed beliefs. The course tends to be chronic, with limited insight and resistance to contrary evidence, distinguishing it from overvalued ideas or mood-congruent beliefs seen in major mood disorders.

patient.stressor: Roughly a year before seeking help, Thanh went through a period of intense stress when her mother developed complications from diabetes, leading Thanh to accompany her to multiple specialist visits and spend long hours in medical settings outside her own clinic job. During this time, she became preoccupied with the idea that certain patients and staff at her high-volume clinic were being selectively exposed to experimental pathogens under the guise of routine bloodwork, initially framed in her mind as a far-fetched but plausible ethical concern. As months passed, this belief became more rigid and elaborate: she started meticulously tracking which patients were sent to which labs, altered her volunteering at community health fairs to "warn" certain groups, and significantly increased her own health-related rituals and avoidance of specific colleagues, yet she continued to function at work well enough that supervisors only saw her as "overly intense." Her family finally urged psychiatric evaluation after she insisted on moving her mother’s care to a distant hospital to avoid a perceived research network and became visibly distressed when relatives and coworkers challenged her firm conviction that a hidden research program was targeting Vietnamese patients.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m convinced some labs are secretly using people like my mom and our community in dangerous experiments, and no one can show me anything that truly proves otherwise.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Over this past year I've become absolutely certain that our hospital and a few connected labs are quietly running some kind of infection experiment on Vietnamese patients—like my mom and many people at my clinic—and no matter how many times people tell me it's impossible, when I see certain names on lab orders, or the same patients being sent to the same outside lab, or my coworkers glancing at each other when I walk by, it just confirms for me that there's a coordinated research program targeting us that everyone else is either too blind or too scared to admit is real.
